recommendations.regimenLabel: Corticosteroid + supportive measures (with stenting / cause-directed therapy)
steps: Sit the patient up; oxygen; assess airway (emergency if stridor/cerebral oedema).
CT chest to define cause and obtain tissue diagnosis before treatment where possible.
Endovascular stenting gives rapid relief, esp. for severe symptoms.
Cause-directed therapy: radiotherapy/chemotherapy for malignancy (SCLC/lymphoma chemo-sensitive).
Corticosteroids in steroid-responsive tumours/airway compromise; anticoagulate if thrombus.

drugRefs.why: Reduces peritumoural/airway oedema in steroid-responsive tumours (lymphoma, thymoma) and airway compromise; avoid before biopsy in suspected lymphoma if it would obscure the diagnosis.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Superior Vena Cava Syndrome / Oncologic Emergencies
ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines — Oncological Emergencies

drugRefs.why: Anticoagulate when SVC obstruction is associated with intraluminal/catheter-related thrombus.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Superior Vena Cava Syndrome / Oncologic Emergencies

decision.label: Tissue diagnosis + stenting/cause-directed therapy; steroid if responsive

confirm: Facial/neck/arm swelling, distended veins, dyspnoea ± plethora; usually malignant. CT confirms level/cause.
